tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. The SRE agent rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving regions on mixed versions. A second attempt finished in all regions. Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate about 0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, look into the orchestrator error that stopped the rollback, and check why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **What I rolled back to:** v2.3.1, the latest release, was unhealthy in production and its staging build (v2.3.1-rc) was too. The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0.
- **Rollback:** The first attempt stopped after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. Rolling back to the same version is safe to repeat, so I tried again, and the second attempt finished. All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0, and the error rate is down from about 18% to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The first request to create it timed out. I retried with the same request ID, which stops a timed-out request from creating a duplicate, so there should be only one incident. The incident notes the failure, the rollback (including the stall partway through), the current state, and three follow-ups:
  - find out why v2.3.1 failed
  - look into the orchestrator error that stopped the rollback
  - find out why a release that failed in staging was put into production

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
Rollback stopped partway: us-east is on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Rolling back to the same target is safe to repeat, so I'll retry once.
